sections.h2: Which McCracken County offices touch a tax bill?
sections.html:
Three do, each with its own lane. A parcel's dollar value is the work of the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA). The Sheriff's Office receives the payment. Only after the spring cutoff does the County Clerk get involved, and then only for bills still open. The PVA's website says outright that it neither mails bills nor accepts payments, so a check carried to the assessment office will be turned around.

You will find the PVA at 621 Washington Street in Paducah. Weekday hours run eight to four-thirty, and callers can dial (270) 444-4712. Public service companies and a few similar accounts are valued in Frankfort by the state Revenue Cabinet instead. For payments, see the Sheriff's tax page, which lists walk-in service Monday to Friday between 8:30 and 4:30 during collection season. County offices share the 300 Clarence Gaines Street address.

sections.h2: When can McCracken County taxes be paid, and what does waiting cost?
sections.html:
Collection by the Sheriff opens November 1 and closes April 15, and the county's delinquent-tax FAQ puts the mailing of notices in late September or early October. KRS 134.015 then prices each stage:

  • Settling the whole bill by November 1 earns 2 percent off, and that date for 2026 is behind us.
  • November 2 to year end: the printed figure, no more and no less.
  • Throughout January, add 5 percent.
  • Once January ends, the add-on doubles to 10 percent.
  • After April 15 the Sheriff hands over whatever is still open.

Mail, phone, counter and a website button (live November through April, per the office) all work. Anyone paying by card or e-check owes a processing charge to an outside vendor, which is shown before you confirm. If a lender escrows your tax, call it first, because the Sheriff sends a bill to the owner only, and the lender may already have requested its own copy.

sections.h2: How much will a McCracken County tax bill come to?
sections.html:
Frankfort's 2025 real property rate is 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents the year before. Run that against the $188,100 Census median and you get about $199.39 for the state alone. The city, schools, library, fire districts and county each add a levy, and the PVA lists those same bodies as users of its assessments.

One line is newer than the rest: a county 911 fee that first appeared on the 2024 bills. Most parcels pay $46.26, the Sheriff says. The early-payment reduction skips that line, which matters when you estimate a credit at closing.

sections.h2: What steps does a McCracken County owner follow to contest a value?
sections.html:
Begin with a sit-down at the PVA office, since nothing can be filed before it. The dates after that are fixed by statute.

  • The roll lies open for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May.
  • Expect the PVA or a deputy to explain the valuation and write up what each side said.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk one business day after the viewing window shuts.
  • Gather proof for the hearing: insurance papers, building costs, land and structure descriptions, and sale listings. A claim with nothing attached is rejected.
  • A panel of local owners hears the case about a month later.

A hired representative has to be on the Revenue Department's list of eligible professionals, such as an attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, with your signed authorization. If bills are already out and the board lands above your claimed figure, a supplemental bill follows. The Sheriff adds a caution of its own: leaving new additions off the record can bring a 20 percent penalty on the bill.

sections.h2: Can older McCracken County owners lower the taxable value?
sections.html:
Yes. Owners 65 and over, and those found totally disabled, can take $49,100 off assessed value for both 2025 and 2026. The rate then applies only to what remains.

Take the $188,100 median: taxable value falls to $139,000, and the state's slice drops to about $147.34. Apply at the McCracken County PVA, not the Sheriff. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Claimants who rely on disability must have a federal or retirement-system finding, and most renew yearly. Veterans with a service-connected disability need not renew yearly, nor do people already ruled permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or the state retirement systems. Nothing is granted until a formal application is on file, the PVA's site notes.

sections.h2: What becomes of an unpaid McCracken County bill when the house is sold?
sections.html:
It stays with the parcel. After April 15 the County Clerk holds it as a certificate of delinquency, records a lien, and charges 1 percent a month. KRS 134.420 lets the lien run 11 years through any change of owner, which means a buyer's title search will turn it up.

Delinquent bills go to the County Attorney, who works under a state agreement. Its letters warn that ignoring the bill can end in foreclosure, while an owner who keeps up an installment agreement has the bill marked unavailable for sale to investors. The Clerk's yearly sale of such bills is normally held in October. An investor who buys one must notify the owner within 50 days, may add its own charges, and can ask a court to foreclose after a year. Before listing, get a payoff figure from the Sheriff, and clear it before April 15 if you can.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about McCracken County itself?
sections.html:
The county spreads over 268 square miles at Kentucky's far western tip, part of the Jackson Purchase, with the Ohio River along its north and the Tennessee River along its northeast. It dates from 1825 and anchors the Paducah, KY-IL metropolitan area. Paducah, the seat, is the lone incorporated city. Farley, Hendron, Massac and Reidland are counted by the Census as designated places, and names such as Lone Oak, Heath and West Paducah show up as unincorporated communities.

Steamboats, barges and the Illinois Central made this a river-and-rail economy, and in the 1920s the railroad put its biggest operating and maintenance base anywhere here. Two districts teach the children: McCracken County Public Schools for nearly everywhere outside the city, and Paducah Public Schools for most of Paducah. West Kentucky Community and Technical College is in town. Clocks run on Central time, and the average worker travels 17.6 minutes to a job.

Owners live in about 69 percent of homes, and 170 permits in 2025 mean most sales involve an existing house. If yours carries unpaid tax, a lien or repairs you would rather skip, an investor paying cash for the house in its current condition can fold the tax payoff into one closing.

faqs.q: Is the McCracken County PVA where I pay my tax?
faqs.a: No. The PVA handles values and exemptions only. Take payment to the Sheriff's Office.

faqs.q: What changes on April 15 for unpaid McCracken County taxes?
faqs.a: Sheriff collection of the prior bill ends that evening. Any balance heads to the County Clerk's office, and interest and fees begin to build.

faqs.q: Is the 911 fee on McCracken County bills eligible for the early-payment cut?
faqs.a: No. According to the Sheriff, the 911 fee that arrived with the 2024 bills sits outside the discount, and most parcels owe $46.26 for it.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead deduction for a McCracken County owner in 2026?
faqs.a: For 2026 the deduction is $49,100, as in 2025. Anyone 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies through the PVA.

faqs.q: Can I close on a McCracken County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The usual route is for the closing agent to pay the balance from the seller's proceeds, after you have asked the Sheriff or Clerk for a payoff.
